direction: March finds persistence through recurring water, a restricted piece of sky and a tree’s offered shade. A sparse tide-edge wash, angular attic drawing and broad warm canopy vary visual density and scale. The sacred encounter, the child’s testimony and the satire of chosen blindness remain text-led.

items.title: The tide returns quietly
items.rationale: Hope follows the tide’s retreat and return. A small advancing edge of water gives that persistence room without a dramatic storm, lighthouse or triumphant sunrise.

review.notes: Pass at normal size: shallow ripple and broken foam line thin naturally into wet sand, earlier wet edge remains faint. Soft grey-blue and sand washes preserve patient return without storm or theatrical sunrise. Foam has slightly more detail in foreground but quieter distance and empty sand support the poem.

items.alt: A small incoming ripple crosses wet sand along a broken edge of foam.

items.title: A sky in fragments
items.rationale: The displaced speaker tries to build a whole sky from the restricted view of an attic. An oblique roof-window glimpse preserves the physical constraint and the longing for openness without inventing a refugee or city.

review.notes: Pass at normal size: inclined roof opening and attached timber divide a small ordinary sky view; continuous framing and ambient light are physically coherent. Wide quiet interior plane carries confinement without fabricated displacement subjects or decorative ruin. Charcoal-gouache texture stays selective and the cloud is incomplete, not a magical portal.

items.alt: A narrow attic roof opening and timber beam divide a glimpse of pale blue sky.

items.title: Shade given in the heat
items.rationale: The speaker recognizes generous feminine care in the gulmohar seen from a balcony. A canopy offering shade preserves that companionship without drawing an idealized woman or repeating a close flower cluster.

review.notes: PASS: broad branching canopy creates believable broken shade on the ground; uneven orange-red blooms and selective feathery foliage support the poem’s generous companionship. Warm open ground gives breathing space. Painted gouache character is retained, with no invented person or documentary location. Floral detail is fuller than the sparse prompt but remains coherent and distinct from the two quiet March images; no material defect. Same-assistant review, independent:false.

items.alt: A spreading gulmohar canopy with orange-red flowers casts broken shade on warm bare ground.

text_led.rationale: The Nabagunjara poem asks the reader to meet unknowability. Preserve the full verbal encounter without generating an unverified hybrid sacred image or replacing historical art.
The child’s testimony of danger must not become a fabricated image of a child beside a corpse; retain the force of the direct voice.
The satire depends on the speaker choosing blindness while injustice continues. Keep the moral discomfort in the words, avoiding a literal blindfolded portrait or invented burning house.
